transcript.text: Dropped a cast iron pan on my ceramic hob and there's a crack right across the front left ring. It still heats up. Can I keep using it until I get a new one?

No — stop using the hob, including the other rings, and isolate it at the cooker switch or consumer unit. A crack right across a ceramic surface can let spillages and moisture reach live electrical parts underneath, creating an electric-shock and further damage risk even though that ring still heats. Do not place pans over the crack or try to seal it with tape, glue or a cover. It needs assessment and repair or replacement by a qualified appliance engineer/electrician; whether the glass top can be replaced depends on the particular hob.

candidates: Cracked ceramic/glass hob surface from impact damage (high)

reading.symptom: crack across the front left ring after a cast iron pan was dropped

plan: They asked: "Can I keep using it until I get a new one?" - answer that first.
The fault they reported is: "crack across the front left ring after a cast iron pan was dropped". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the one or two safe checks, or the one question, that would best tell those causes apart. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.
